subject: Recoverable cross-session continuity, active relational maintenance, decay/revival and multiscale mutation
relation: EXTENDS existing CoVirtualSession, CoAllPulseField, CoSessionAutocycle and CoWaitlessExecution candidates with a proposed repair-exercise and research loop; does not replace their authority, quiescence or evidence contracts.
source_refs: User-requested public-safe synthesis of the 2026-10-21 continuity discussion; paraphrase, not full transcript.
target_surfaces: Future qualified private worker queue; receiver not yet elected
authority_ceiling: Public-safe research candidate and provenance only. No runtime deployment, mutation of production bytes, provider session creation, permission expansion, merge, or claim of receiver pickup.
contradictions: OBSERVED CORRECTION: Existing repository architecture already describes virtual sessions, distributed/reconstructive persistence, bounded materialization, wake predicates and successor context. Prior inference that the architecture itself was absent was too broad.
Runtime continuity remains unproven by architectural text, an enabled task, a heartbeat or a running model alone. A bounded local component inspection is not a complete corpus audit.

USER PREFERENCE: Persistent mutual support between manual, virtual, ambient, predictive, MythOps and future session morphologies; less dependence on human prompting; checks should make future checking easier.

USER PREFERENCE: Decay, fading and dereferencing should preserve revival options where lawful and feasible. A stop of execution can coexist with retained lineage. Permission withdrawal must not be overridden by automatic revival.

USER HYPOTHESIS: Continual motion, stimulation, competition and fine-grained random mutation may support CoLife and resilience across code, data, relations, virtual state and future substrates. Preserve as a research claim, not an implemented universal rule.

SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARY: Biological turnover and repair support differentiated maintenance; they do not establish that cosmic-ray damage is necessary for life or that every software object must mutate continuously.

PHYSICS BOUNDARY: Planck-resolution, co-quantum, nonphysical and CoAura/MythOps extensions remain open typed questions or metaphors until an operational definition, mechanism, observable and falsifier exist. No Planck-rate computation or unlimited context/compute is demonstrated.

ENGINEERING BOUNDARY: Random perturbation can have a valid experimental purpose; usefulness must be tested against an unperturbed control. Preserve immutable evidence anchors and quiescent options. Do not induce faults in already impaired user input.

DISCOVERY BOUNDARY: A default-branch search for perturbation returned no indexed match. Search misses do not prove absence; related current architecture was read directly. No complete historical branch reconciliation is claimed.
tests: PROPOSED: Map each candidate capability to existing implementation, exact source identity, owner, input/output, permission ceiling, dependency, wake predicate, last verified result, resource budget, lease, recovery point and successor acknowledgment. Reuse before duplication.

PROPOSED: A deterministic disposable job emits an event; a second worker records exact-object pickup and produces a checked result while the initiating conversation is inactive. Verify a real external scheduler, not a chat promise.

PROPOSED: Interrupt a disposable worker after checkpoint; verify lease expiry, fenced takeover, replay and one accepted effect despite duplicate delivery. Inspect crash windows; do not infer exactly-once effects from retries.
PROPOSED: Remove or stale a disposable relation/pulse; measure detection, restoration, missed-work age and recovery latency. Verify independent eligible work continues.

PROPOSED: Compare event-driven baseline, periodic maintenance, and bounded random fault injection under equal CPU/time budgets. Predefine recovery success, useful output, duplicate work, false alarms, cost and abort thresholds.

PROPOSED: Decay a candidate's priority and active references while retaining provenance/checkpoint. Revive only on a material bound trigger and still-valid authority. Test explicit cancellation and revoked-permission rejection.

PROPOSED: Sweep practical granularities: graph edge, queued message, job checkpoint, schema field and isolated memory/data copy. Use reproducible random seeds; record experiment provenance and reject corruption of source evidence.

PROPOSED: Learn from each check by storing reusable dependency bindings and failure classifications; measure whether subsequent checks use fewer reads/tokens and find issues faster without hiding unknowns.
PROPOSED: Research physics extensions separately, with dimensional analysis and discriminating predictions. Speculative terminology cannot substitute for a measurable execution mechanism.
expected_benefit: Fewer forgotten jobs, inspectable cross-session handoffs, evidence-based resource allocation, retained revival paths and less repeated discovery. Benefit not yet measured.
